Brightwater Logistics - Paid Parental Leave Policy (excerpt)
Section 4. Eligibility. An employee qualifies for 16 weeks of paid parental leave only if all four conditions below are met.
4.1 Tenure: on the expected date of birth or placement, the employee has been directly employed by Brightwater for at least 12 continuous months. Time spent working at Brightwater through a staffing agency does not count toward tenure.
4.2 Hours: the employee is scheduled for at least 20 hours per week.
4.3 Employment type: the employee is on Brightwater's own payroll, not an independent contractor or agency worker.
4.4 Notice: the leave request is submitted at least 8 weeks before the planned start date of the leave.

HR case file PL-2025-031
Lucia Ferrand worked in Brightwater's Tacoma warehouse through the staffing agency Quillon Staffing from June 2024 until Brightwater hired her directly onto its payroll on 1 March 2025. She is scheduled for 24 hours per week as an inventory coordinator. Her baby is due on 15 February 2026. On 20 November 2025 she submitted a request for parental leave starting 2 February 2026. Her manager supports the request and describes Lucia as having been 'part of the Tacoma team for well over a year.'

questions.instruction: Which Section 4 eligibility conditions does Lucia meet?

candidates.description: 4.1: at least 12 continuous months of direct Brightwater employment by the expected birth date
4.2: scheduled for at least 20 hours per week
4.3: on Brightwater's own payroll rather than a contractor or agency worker
4.4: leave requested at least 8 weeks before the planned start date

questions.notes: Direct hire on 1 Mar 2025 gives under 12 months by the 15 Feb 2026 due date; 24 hours, payroll, 74 days' notice.

questions.instruction: Which of the policy's four requirements are satisfied in Lucia Ferrand's case?

candidates.description: Tenure: 12 or more continuous months directly employed by Brightwater as of the due date, agency time excluded
Hours: a schedule of 20 or more hours each week
Employment type: paid through Brightwater's payroll, not via an agency or as a contractor
Notice: leave request made 8 or more weeks ahead of the leave start

questions.notes: Agency months do not count, so tenure is about 11.5 months; the other three requirements are met.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, does Lucia qualify for paid parental leave?
questions.notes: Fails 4.1: direct employment began 1 March 2025, under 12 months before the 15 February 2026 due date.

12.1 Rent is due on the 1st day of each month. If the Tenant pays rent more than 5 days after the due date, the Tenant owes a late fee of $40.
12.2 Within 21 days after the Tenant moves out and returns all keys, the Landlord must either refund the full security deposit or send the Tenant an itemized statement of deductions together with the remaining balance.
12.3 If the Landlord misses the 21-day deadline in 12.2, the Landlord loses the right to make any deductions and must refund the entire deposit.
12.4 Permitted deductions are limited to unpaid rent, unpaid fees, and damage beyond normal wear and tear.

Property manager's notes: Tenant Ruth Okafor paid her July rent on July 10. She moved out on July 31 and handed in all keys the same day. Her security deposit was $1,500. questions.instruction: Under the lease, does the landlord owe a late fee?
questions.notes: Clause 12.1 late fees are owed by the tenant; the landlord's missed deadline only forfeits deductions under 12.3.

questions.instruction: Did Ruth incur the $40 late fee under clause 12.1?
questions.notes: July rent was due July 1 and paid July 10, more than 5 days late.

questions.instruction: Under the lease, how much of the deposit must the landlord refund to Ruth?

candidates.description: $1,160: the deposit minus both deductions
$1,200: the deposit minus only the carpet-cleaning deduction
$1,460: the deposit minus only the late-fee deduction
$1,500: the entire deposit

questions.notes: Statement mailed August 26, 26 days after the July 31 move-out; the 21-day deadline was missed, so no deductions are allowed.

WAYVANE TRIP PROTECTION - Policy Wording, Plan TP-Gold (policies purchased on or after 1 September 2025)

PART A - DEFINITIONS
Trip cost: the prepaid, non-refundable payments for travel arrangements that the insured declared when buying this policy.
Travel companion: a person booked on the same itinerary as the insured.
Immediate family member: a spouse or domestic partner, parent, child, sibling or grandparent of the insured.
Pre-existing condition: any illness, injury or medical condition for which the insured received diagnosis, treatment or medication during the 60 days immediately before the policy purchase date.

PART B - SUMMARY OF COVER
Trip cancellation: up to 100% of trip cost.
Cancel For Any Reason (CFAR) rider, optional: up to 75% of trip cost. The rider can only be added if the policy is bought within 14 days of the first trip payment.
Baggage delay: up to $300 for essential purchases after a delay of 12 hours or more.
Emergency medical expenses: up to $50,000 per insured.

PART C - DECLARING MEDICAL CONDITIONS
When buying this policy, the insured must declare every pre-existing condition. A declared pre-existing condition is covered only if the insured also pays the medical screening premium shown in the quote.

PART D - HOW CANCELLATION CLAIMS ARE DECIDED
The claims team applies the rules below in the order listed. The first rule that applies decides the claim, and no later rule is considered.
Rule 1. If the claim is submitted more than 90 days after the date the trip was cancelled, the claim is denied.
Rule 2. If the cancellation results from a pre-existing condition that was not declared under Part C, the claim is denied.
Rule 3. If the trip was cancelled because of (a) sickness or injury of the insured or a travel companion, certified in writing by a physician as preventing travel, (b) the death of an immediate family member, or (c) an official evacuation order covering the destination, the insurer reimburses 100% of trip cost.
Rule 4. If the insured holds the CFAR rider and cancelled more than 48 hours before the scheduled departure, the insurer reimburses 75% of trip cost.
Rule 5. In all other cases, the claim is denied.

PART E - DOCUMENTS
A cancellation claim must include the booking invoice, proof of cancellation from each travel supplier, and any supporting medical or official documents. Missing documents delay a decision but do not change which rule applies.

CLAIM FILE MTP-26-04417
Insured: Tomasz Wierzbicki. Plan TP-Gold with CFAR rider, purchased 3 January 2026; first trip payment made 28 December 2025. Pre-existing conditions declared at purchase: none.
Trip: 10-day guided walking holiday in Madeira for two, departing 20 March 2026. Declared trip cost: $4,200.
Adjuster notes: The insured's brother, Pawel, was booked on the same itinerary but holds a separate policy with another insurer; his claim is not part of this file. On 15 December 2025 the insured strained his lower back while moving furniture and was treated by a physiotherapist the same day; he had no further treatment or medication for it until March 2026. He reports that his back felt fine through January and February and that he kept up his training walks. On 9 March 2026 the pain returned severely. On 10 March his physician, Dr. Anneliese Roth, certified in writing that he was unfit to travel because of a recurrence of the back strain. He cancelled the trip with the tour operator on 11 March 2026 and submitted this claim on 2 April 2026, attaching the physician's letter, the booking invoice and the operator's cancellation confirmation. The operator refunded nothing, so the full $4,200 is claimed.

questions.instruction: Which outcome do the Part D rules prescribe for claim MTP-26-04417?

candidates.description: Denied under Rule 1 (claim submitted too late)
Denied under Rule 2 (undeclared pre-existing condition)
100% of trip cost reimbursed under Rule 3
75% of trip cost reimbursed under Rule 4 (CFAR rider)
Denied under Rule 5 (no earlier rule applies)

questions.notes: Back strain treated 15 Dec 2025, 19 days before purchase, and undeclared; Rule 2 applies first, so Rules 3 and 4 are never reached.

questions.instruction: Under the policy wording, will Tomasz be reimbursed 75% of his trip cost under the CFAR rider?
questions.notes: Rule 2 decides the claim before Rule 4 is considered, so no CFAR reimbursement is paid.

questions.instruction: Does Tomasz's back strain meet the policy's definition of a pre-existing condition?
questions.notes: Treated on 15 December 2025, within the 60 days before the 3 January 2026 purchase date.

Lotmark Marketplace - Order Rules (excerpt)
Buyer duties: The winning bidder must pay within 2 calendar days after the auction ends. If the buyer has not paid by then, the seller may cancel the order and report an unpaid-item strike against the buyer. A buyer who collects three unpaid-item strikes within 12 months is suspended.
Seller duties: The seller must ship the item within 3 business days after receiving payment; business days are Monday to Friday. If the item has not shipped by the end of the third business day, the buyer may cancel the order and receive a full refund. The seller must also answer buyer messages within 48 hours.

Order TW-55810 - event log
Sat 6 June 2026, 21:14 - Auction for a used twin-lens reflex camera ends. Winning bidder (buyer): ella_frames. Seller: lenshouse_raj.
Mon 8 June, 09:02 - ella_frames pays $412.
Mon 8 June, 10:30 - ella_frames messages the seller asking for tracking details once the camera ships.
Tue 9 June, 08:15 - lenshouse_raj replies: 'Will ship this week, promise!'
Fri 12 June, 18:00 - No shipping label has been created yet.
Sat 13 June, 11:40 - ella_frames asks Lotmark to cancel the order. The camera still has not shipped.

questions.instruction: Under the order rules, may ella_frames cancel the order and receive a full refund?
questions.notes: Paid Monday 8 June; the third business day, Thursday 11 June, ended without shipment, so the buyer may cancel for a full refund.

questions.instruction: What consequence do the order rules impose on the buyer, ella_frames, for this order?

candidates.description: The seller may report an unpaid-item strike against her
Her account is suspended
None of the above: the rules impose no consequence on the buyer for this order

questions.notes: She paid about 36 hours after the auction ended, within 2 days; the only breach was the seller's.

candidates.description: The buyer did not pay within 2 calendar days after the auction ended
The seller did not ship within 3 business days after payment
The seller did not answer a buyer message within 48 hours
